messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Our team needs a rocket design. Target about 700 m; recovery matters most to me, so under 6 m/s at touchdown. A single chute is fine. Plan for 6 m/s wind.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee about 700 m (approximate, within 5%, so about 665 to 735 m). Landing at most 6 m/s (maximum), and the user says recovery matters most. A single chute (fixed), not dual deploy. Wind is 6 m/s (fixed). Rail, angle and site are not stated, so a 1.5 m rail, vertical, sea level. Single stage.
2. Feasibility: no-drag speed for 700 m is sqrt(2*9.81*700) = 117 m/s. A light F can get close and a small G will overshoot unless the rocket is heavier. 6 m/s of wind is under the 8.94 m/s cap, but it will weathercock, so I should not run the margin up near 3 cal. I need impulse and thrust for an F and a G before I commit.

2. Feasibility: the F15 is only 49.6 N*s and 14.5 N average, soft for 700 m. The G64W is 118 N*s and the G80T is 135.6 N*s, both likely to fly well past the 5% band in a light tube. The Estes F50 is 76.8 N*s at 55.8 N average, a 29 mm case (0.029 m by 0.098 m, 0.0836 kg) with a single 6 s delay. That impulse is the closest match, and the thrust is healthy on a 1.5 m rail.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.18 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 55.8 / (0.18 * 9.81) = 31.6. Pad weight 0.18 * 9.81 = 1.77 N, rail acceleration (55.8 - 1.77) / 0.18 = 300 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 300 * 1.5) = 30 m/s. Propellant is 0.038 kg, descent mass 0.18 - 0.038 = 0.14 kg. Recovery is the priority, so I size the chute for 4.5 m/s rather than 6: area 2 * 0.14 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4.5^2) = 0.138 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.138 / 3.1416) = 0.42 m. I will use 0.55 m. Burn is 1.37 s, so the 6 s delay ejects near 7.4 s, which may be a little early for a 700 m coast.
4. Draft: 0.12 m ogive polystyrene nose on a 0.50 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.041 m, wall 0.8 mm. Mount 0.032 m outside, 0.11 m long, Estes F50 with the 6 s delay. Three balsa fins, root 0.080 m, tip 0.035 m, span 0.055 m, sweep 0.040 m, 3 mm thick. One 0.55 m polyethylene chute on ejection. Wind 6 m/s.

4. Check: altitude landed in the band and the landing is slow, but the rocket is neutral. The simulator gives 695.2 m, and (700 - 695.2) / 700 = 0.7% low, inside 5%. Landing is 3.1 m/s, rail exit 37.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight 37.5. Stability is 0.0 cal at rail exit and 0.0 cal through the burn, which fails both the 1 cal launch gate and the requirement to stay above 0. The chute opens at 7.4 s, just before the 7.79 s apogee. Mass is 0.152 kg. Wind is 6 m/s. Drift is 1,307 m; the request does not cap it.
5. Fix: the failing value is 0.0 cal. The fins are too small for a 29 mm motor in a 41 mm tube. I am enlarging only the balsa fins: root 0.080 m to 0.11 m, tip 0.035 m to 0.045 m, span 0.055 m to 0.080 m, sweep 0.040 m to 0.055 m. Apogee has only a little room above the bottom of the band (695.2 m versus about 665 m), so I am not also adding nose mass.

4. Check: the bigger fins helped and they were not enough. The simulator gives 0.61 cal at rail exit and through the burn, still under 1.0 cal. Apogee fell to 635.6 m, and (700 - 635.6) / 700 = 9.2% low, outside the 5% band. Landing 3.1 m/s, rail exit 36.7 m/s and thrust-to-weight 36.4 still pass. Mass is 0.157 kg. I need the CG and CP before I add nose mass, because another fin increase will cost more of the altitude.

4. Check: on the pad the margin is already 1.1 cal. CG is 0.469 m, CP is 0.514 m, diameter 0.041 m. The flight number was lower: 0.61 cal at rail exit. So the pad reading is optimistic by about half a caliber, and the flight is what fails. Apogee is still 635.6 m.
5. Fix: flight margin 0.61 cal is under 1.0, and 635.6 m is under the band. I want the pad CG near 0.444 m so the pad margin is about 1.7 cal and the flight number still clears 1. Clay of 0.012 kg at the top of the tube, about 0.12 m from the nose tip, gives (0.157 * 0.469 + 0.012 * 0.12) / (0.157 + 0.012) = 0.444 m, and (0.514 - 0.444) / 0.041 = 1.71 cal on the pad. With that CG I can give some fin area back to recover altitude: root 0.090 m, tip 0.038 m, span 0.065 m, sweep 0.045 m, and I am shortening the tube from 0.50 m to 0.42 m. Chute and F50 stay.

4. Check: altitude is back in the band. The simulator gives 697.1 m, and (700 - 697.1) / 700 = 0.4% low. Landing 3.2 m/s, rail exit 36.1 m/s, thrust-to-weight 35.6. The margin did not follow the pad estimate: rail exit is 0.69 cal and the burn minimum is 0.69 cal, still under 1.0. Shrinking the fins moved the CP forward and ate most of the clay. Mass is 0.16 kg.
5. Fix: the failing value is 0.69 cal. Apogee can spare a little mass, since 697.1 m sits near the middle of the band and the floor is about 665 m. I am only increasing the nose clay, from 0.012 kg to 0.028 kg, at the same spot. Fins, tube and F50 stay, so the drag that just recovered the altitude stays put.

4. Check: the extra clay fixed the margin and, in this wind, the altitude went up rather than down. The simulator gives 716.7 m, and (716.7 - 700) / 700 = 2.4% high, still inside 5%. Rail-exit margin is 1.25 cal and the burn minimum is 1.25 cal. Landing is 3.4 m/s, rail exit 35.0 m/s, thrust-to-weight 32.3. The single chute opens at 7.4 s, just before the 7.85 s apogee, at 16.3 m/s. Touchdown is still slow. Wind is 6 m/s. Mass is 0.176 kg.
5. Fix: no further change. Altitude, the single chute, the landing speed and the stability gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 716.7 m is toward the top of the band. Less nose clay weathercocked more in the 6 m/s wind and flew lower, so a lighter build is not automatically higher. The 6 s delay opens the canopy at 16.3 m/s, which is harder on the chute than the 3.4 m/s landing suggests. Margin is 1.25 cal, with some room, but the result is sensitive to where that 0.028 kg actually sits. Drift is over a kilometre; the request did not limit it.
messages.content:
Estes F50-6 in a 41 mm cardboard rocket with 0.028 kg of nose clay and one 0.55 m chute.
In 6 m/s wind it reaches 716.7 m, about 2% over 700 m, leaves the rail at 35 m/s, and lands at 3.4 m/s. Margin is 1.25 cal.
The 6 s delay opens the chute at 16.3 m/s, slightly before apogee. Touchdown itself is well under 6 m/s.
